summary.text: A solid is a state of matter in which atoms are closely packed and are difficult to move past each other.
Solids resist compression, expansion and forces that would change their shape, and unlike liquids they do not flow to take the shape of a container.
The atoms in a solid are tightly bound either in regular geometric lattices, called crystalline, or in irregular arrangements, called amorphous.

facts.label: How they form
facts.value: A fluid cooled below its melting point becomes solid

facts.label: Melting range
facts.value: From 0.10 K for helium-3 to around 4,100 K at 1 atm

facts.label: Density
facts.value: Most solids are denser than their liquids and sink in them

facts.label: Field of study
facts.value: Solid-state physics, a major branch of condensed matter physics

items.prompt: You compare a tiny ice cube with a huge block of ice at the same pressure. How do their melting temperatures compare?

options.label: The block melts at a higher temperature, because it holds more heat
They match, because melting point does not depend on how much matter there is
The cube melts at a higher temperature, because it is denser
The block melts at a lower temperature, because it has more surface

items.explain: The melting point is an intrinsic property of a substance, independent of how much of it there is.

items.prompt: A hiker steps onto loose lunar dust and feels it give way, though each grain is solid. Why does it feel soft?

options.label: The grains are made of a softer material than solid rock
The dust is really a liquid that has been broken into pieces
The grains can slip past one another easily
Each grain compresses a lot under the hiker's weight

items.explain: In aggregates such as sand or lunar dust, particles slip past one another, though changes in individual particles are greatly hindered. This gives a perceived softness.

items.prompt: A jeweler examines a metal ring and a glass bead under a powerful microscope. How are the atoms arranged?

options.label: Both have atoms in a regular lattice, but glass is looser
The metal's atoms are irregular, while the glass's form a regular lattice
Both have irregular atoms, because all solids are disordered
The metal's atoms form a regular lattice, while the glass's atoms have no regular pattern

items.explain: Metals are crystalline solids with regular geometric lattices, while glass is an amorphous solid with an irregular arrangement.

items.prompt: An empty syringe plugged at the tip squeezes down easily when full of air. Why can't you squeeze a solid plug the same way?

options.label: Gas molecules are far apart with few interactions, while a solid's atoms resist being pushed closer
A solid's atoms are lighter than gas molecules and so push back harder
Gas molecules bond into a rigid lattice when they are pushed together
Solids have no spaces between atoms, so their atoms melt when pushed

items.explain: Gases are easily compressed because their molecules are far apart with few intermolecular interactions, while non-porous solids strongly resist compression.

items.prompt: A steel rod is heated, well below its melting point. What happens to its size?

options.label: It stays exactly the same, because solids are rigid
It expands, but much less than a liquid or gas would
It shrinks, because the atoms pack tighter as they warm
It expands by the same amount as a gas would

items.explain: Solids expand when heated, as thermal energy increases the distance between atoms, but they do so to a much lesser extent than the other phases.

items.prompt: An iceberg floats on the sea. What does this tell you?

options.label: Ice is less rigid than most solids, so it can float
Solids normally float on their liquids, and ice is typical
Water is an exception to the usual rule that a solid sinks in its own liquid
The ice must contain trapped air, as all solids do

items.explain: For the vast majority of substances the solid is denser than the liquid and sinks in it. Water is an exception, and ice is less dense than water.
